result:
What a fascinating and thought-provoking question! If I could change the world in one way, I would choose to make access to clean water and sanitation a universal reality.

Imagine a world where every person, regardless of their geographical location, socio-economic status, or background, has access to clean drinking water and proper sanitation facilities. A world where no one has to walk miles to fetch water, or drink contaminated water that can cause diseases. A world where sanitation is a basic human right, and everyone has a safe and hygienic place to go.

According to the United Nations, over 2 billion people worldwide lack access to safely managed drinking water services, and 4.2 billion people lack access to safely managed sanitation services. This results in millions of deaths every year from water-borne diseases, and countless hours spent by people, especially women and children, collecting water instead of engaging in productive activities.

If I could change the world in one way, I would make sure that every person has access to clean water and sanitation, 24/7, without having to worry about the distance, cost, or availability. This would have a ripple effect on many aspects of life, including:

* Improved health: Reduced incidence of water-borne diseases, and a decrease in mortality rates.
* Increased productivity: People, especially women and children, would have more time to engage in education, work, and other activities that can improve their socio-economic status.
* Enhanced dignity: Every person would have access to basic human rights, and would be able to live with dignity.
* Environmental benefits: Proper sanitation and waste management would reduce pollution and protect ecosystems.

That's my one change to make the world a better place!
